business_model.claim: CF Industries produces anhydrous ammonia from atmospheric nitrogen and natural gas using the Haber-Bosch process and sells ammonia or upgraded nitrogen products including granular urea, UAN, AN, DEF, urea liquor, nitric acid, and aqua ammonia.
quotes: At our core, CF Industries is a producer of ammonia.
We use the Haber-Bosch process to fix atmospheric nitrogen with hydrogen from natural gas to produce anhydrous ammonia, whose chemical composition is NH3.
Products derived from ammonia that are most often used as nitrogen fertilizers include granular urea, urea ammonium nitrate solution (UAN) and ammonium nitrate (AN).
Products derived from ammonia that are sold primarily to industrial customers include diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), urea liquor, nitric acid and aqua ammonia.

business_model.claim: CF's nitrogen products are global commodities with little or no product differentiation, so selling prices fluctuate with global supply and demand and must generally incent high-cost marginal producers to operate at or above breakeven.
quotes: The nitrogen products that we produce are global commodities or are derived from global commodities, with little or no product differentiation.

Customers tend to make their purchasing decisions of these products principally on the basis of delivered price and, to a lesser extent, low-carbon attributes, reliability, customer service and product quality.

In general, the prevailing global prices for nitrogen products must be at a level to incent the high-cost marginal producer to produce product at a breakeven or above price, or else they would cease production and leave a portion of global demand unsatisfied.

business_model.claim: In 2025, CF's average selling price increased 19% from $313 per ton in 2024 to $372 per ton, raising net sales by approximately $1.06 billion, while 1% higher sales volume of 19.1 million tons increased net sales by approximately $84 million.
quotes: The average selling price for our products was $372 per ton in 2025 compared to $313 per ton in 2024.
The 19% increase in the average selling price for our products in 2025 compared to 2024 resulted in a year-over-year increase in net sales of approximately $1.06 billion.
We shipped 19.1 million tons of product in 2025 compared to 18.9 million tons in 2024.
This resulted in an increase in net sales of approximately $84 million for 2025 compared to 2024.

business_model.claim: Fertilizer demand is driven by planted acreage, crop selection, grain inventories, farm economics, and U.S. ethanol demand (representing approximately 35% of total U.S. corn demand), with North American demand peaking during spring planting and again after fall harvest.
quotes: Demand for nitrogen products is affected by planted acreage, crop selection and fertilizer application rates, driven by population changes, economic growth, changes in dietary habits and non-food use of crops, such as production of ethanol and other biofuels.

For example, ethanol production in the United States contributes significantly to corn demand, representing approximately 35% of total U.S. corn demand, and is impacted by federal legislation mandating renewable fuels use.
The strongest demand for our products in North America occurs during the spring planting season, with a second period of strong demand following the fall harvest.

business_model.claim: Global trade flows and regional pricing are influenced by tariffs, anti-dumping duties, and export policies, including Chinese export limits, EU tariffs on Russian nitrogen fertilizers, and EU anti-dumping duties on UAN from Russia, Trinidad, and the United States extended through January 6, 2031.
quotes: China, the world’s largest producer and consumer of nitrogen fertilizers, currently has a government policy to limit exports of nitrogen fertilizers through a variety of measures.

For example, the imposition of duties, tariffs or quotas in a region, such as the European Union’s imposition of additional and increasing tariffs on nitrogen fertilizers from Russia that began in July 2025, can directly impact product pricing in that region, which can lead to changes in global trade flows and impact the global supply and demand balance and pricing.

For example, the European Commission recently extended through January 6, 2031, definitive anti-dumping duties on imports to the European Union (EU) of UAN manufactured in Russia, Trinidad and the United States.

business_model.claim: Natural gas serves as both feedstock and fuel and is CF's largest and most volatile manufacturing cost, representing approximately 34% of production costs in 2025 and 28% in 2024, with all ammonia plants located in the United States and Canada.
quotes: Natural gas is the largest and most volatile component of the manufacturing cost for our nitrogen products, representing approximately 34% and 28%, respectively, of our production costs in 2025 and 2024.
All of our ammonia manufacturing plants are located in the United States and Canada.

In recent years, the cost of North American natural gas for the production of nitrogen fertilizers has been significantly lower than the cost of natural gas in other parts of the world where the industry’s marginal nitrogen producers are located.

business_model.claim: Manufacturing and distribution costs also depend on third-party electricity and pipeline utilities (with certain plants reliant on a single natural gas pipeline), leased railcars, and third-party rail, barge, truck, and vessel transport, which can be disrupted or made costlier by low water levels and severe weather.
quotes: We use raw materials, primarily natural gas, and utilities, such as electricity, in the manufacture of our nitrogen products.

Our natural gas is transported by pipeline to our facilities by third party transportation providers or through the use of facilities owned by third parties, and certain of our plants are reliant on only one natural gas pipeline.
In addition, we rely on railroad, barge, truck, vessel and pipeline companies to coordinate and deliver finished products to our distribution system and to ship finished products to our customers.
For example, recent low water levels on the U.S. river system and in the Panama Canal have delayed shipping in these locations, resulting in an increase in shipping costs.

business_model.claim: CF's Donaldsonville, planned Yazoo City, and Blue Point carbon capture projects qualify or are expected to qualify for Section 45Q tax credits per metric ton of carbon dioxide permanently stored, while non-IEEPA tariffs on steel and aluminum imports may raise capital equipment costs at Blue Point.
quotes: The project qualifies for tax credits under Section 45Q of the Internal Revenue Code (45Q Tax Credits), which provide a tax credit per metric ton of CO2 captured and disposed of in secure geological storage.

The Supreme Court decision did not modify non-IEEPA tariffs, including tariffs on imports of certain steel and aluminum products and their derivatives which may impact the cost of our capital equipment, including for development and construction at our Blue Point complex.

competitive_position.claim: North America's accessibility exposes CF Industries to import competition from the Middle East, Trinidad, Africa, and Russia, potential increases in Chinese fertilizer exports, EU anti-dumping duties on U.S. UAN, and U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs affecting capital project costs.
quotes: North America, where we manufacture and sell most of our products, is one of the largest and most accessible nitrogen trading regions in the world.
In addition, in recent years, high volumes of urea ammonium nitrate solution (UAN) imports from Russia have negatively affected U.S. producers’ UAN profitability.
China, the world’s largest producer and consumer of nitrogen fertilizers, currently has a government policy to limit exports of nitrogen fertilizers through a variety of measures.

For example, the European Commission recently extended through January 6, 2031, definitive anti-dumping duties on imports to the European Union (EU) of UAN manufactured in Russia, Trinidad and the United States.

The Supreme Court decision did not modify non-IEEPA tariffs, including tariffs on imports of certain steel and aluminum products and their derivatives which may impact the cost of our capital equipment, including for development and construction at our Blue Point complex.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors [P2].
competitive_position.claim: Long-term nitrogen demand faces threats from potential reductions in corn-based ethanol mandates (which drive approximately 35% of total U.S. corn demand), shifts toward soybean acreage, nitrogen-fixing or nitrogen-efficient crop technologies, and government restrictions on fertilizer emissions such as Canada's 30% reduction target.
quotes: For example, ethanol production in the United States contributes significantly to corn demand, representing approximately 35% of total U.S. corn demand, and is impacted by federal legislation mandating renewable fuels use.

Developments in crop technology, such as nitrogen fixation, the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into compounds that plants can assimilate, or nitrogen-efficient varieties, or developments in alternatives to traditional animal feed or alternative proteins, could also reduce the use of nitrogen fertilizers and adversely affect the demand for our products.

In addition, Canada has announced a target of reducing emissions from fertilizers by 30% below 2020 levels by 2030 and is supporting implementation through improved nitrogen management and optimizing fertilizer use.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors [P2] and Q3 2026 earnings release [P5].
competitive_position.claim: Operations and distribution face threats from extreme weather (including hurricanes near Donaldsonville and Waggaman and low river water levels), single-pipeline gas dependence at certain plants, third-party CO2 sequestration reliance, and facility outages such as the Yazoo City Complex suspension.
quotes: Our Donaldsonville and Waggaman complexes are located in an area of the United States that experiences a relatively high level of hurricane or high wind activity and several of our complexes are located in areas that experience extreme weather events for which insurance may be insufficient or unavailable.

Our natural gas is transported by pipeline to our facilities by third party transportation providers or through the use of facilities owned by third parties, and certain of our plants are reliant on only one natural gas pipeline.

Available ammonia capacity represents CF Industries’ average annual gross ammonia capacity of its manufacturing network, as described in the Company's 2025 Form 10-K, less the average gross ammonia capacity of its Yazoo City Complex, which management currently expects will resume operations in 1H 2027

The EO directs the Attorney General and the Federal Trade Commission to each establish a Food Supply Chain Security Task Force to investigate price-fixing and anti-competitive practices across the sector, including fertilizer, and take action as necessary, including bringing enforcement actions and proposing new regulatory approaches.

risks.basis: Stated in 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A (P2) and Item 7 (P3), with hedging disclosures in Q3 2026 earnings release (P5).
risks.claim: Natural gas represented approximately 34% of production costs in 2025, exposing earnings to North American gas price volatility and potential erosion of regional energy cost differentials.
quotes: Natural gas is the largest and most volatile component of the manufacturing cost for our nitrogen products, representing approximately 34% and 28%, respectively, of our production costs in 2025 and 2024.

If natural gas prices outside of North America were to decrease or North American natural gas prices were to increase, our favorable energy cost differentials relative to the industry’s marginal nitrogen producers could significantly erode, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

risks.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A (P4), Q3 2026 earnings release (P5), 2025 Form 10-K (P1, P3), and 10-Q balance sheet (F1).
risks.claim: Construction of the Blue Point One low-carbon ammonia facility, estimated at approximately $3.7 billion, carries risks of cost overruns, tariffs on imported materials, schedule delays, and technology performance.
quotes: We estimate that the cost of the Blue Point One joint venture’s low-carbon ATR ammonia production facility with CCS technologies will be approximately $3.7 billion.

We anticipate that approximately one-third of the estimated cost is related to materials that will be imported to the United States, with the majority of imported materials expected to arrive in Louisiana in 2028.

risks.basis: Stated in 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A (P2), with demand diversification stated in P1, P3, and P4.
risks.claim: Agricultural demand for nitrogen products could fall if U.S. corn-based ethanol mandates weaken, soybean acreage expands, crop technology lowers nitrogen use, or governments restrict fertilizer application.
quotes: Any reduction in the demand for our nitrogen fertilizer products, including as a result of technological developments or limitations on the use and application of nitrogen fertilizers, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

risks.basis: Stated in 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A (P2), with distribution and customer-advance context in P1, P4, and F1.

risks.claim: CF Industries depends on third-party pipelines, utilities, transport, and carbon dioxide sequestration providers, while its Yazoo City Complex is offline pending a restart.
quotes: Any delay or interruption in the delivery of raw materials or utilities, even for a limited period, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
